root_idea.summary: A root centered on falling or being thrown into disturbance with an accompanying sound.
root_idea.development: The semantic field extends from audible falling and collapse to the sounds of water, wind, and breathing, with related developments in descent, movement, and places or openings into which things fall.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quranic group is the Form I verb خَرَّ, normalized as the standard perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To fall or fall down, especially from a higher to a lower place; originally, to fall with an audible impact or sound.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for physical falling, collapse, and descent. The audible element is explicit in the lexical explanation of the verb's original usage but is not required in every later use.

senses.definition: To fall prostrate or bow down in submission.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in constructions such as خَرَّ لِلّٰهِ سَاجِدًا, خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا, and خَرُّوا لِلْأَذْقَانِ. In the Quranic prostration construction, the falling is associated with glorification and praise.

senses.definition: To die, figuratively understood as falling down.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative tropical interpretation of a Quranic passage discussed in the lexical evidence; the same passage is also explained as physical falling, so this is not the ordinary sense of every Quranic occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a murmuring, rumbling, gurgling, rustling, or rattling sound, of water, wind, an eagle's wings, or breathing during sleep; also of the sound made in strangulation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be water, wind, a flying bird, a sleeping person or animal, or a person suffering strangulation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stumble after going right or following the proper course.
For sins to fall away, depart, or be removed.
To roll or tumble down from a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or an inanimate object such as a stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come down or descend from one place to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A motion use distinct from literal falling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come upon someone suddenly or unawares from an unknown place.
To come from one town, country, or other place to another, or to pass along, away, or by.
To be confounded or stupefied by shame, becoming speechless and motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Restricted to the idiomatic expressions خَرَرْتَ عَنْ يَدَيْكَ and خَرَرْتَ مِنْ يَدَيْكِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause an arm or hand to fall by a stroke of the sword.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly used of a person or of the belly. Form VII usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the belly to quiver or shake about because of bigness or leanness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form II quadriliteralized usage concerning the belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mouth or opening of a mill or millstone into which grain is thrown.
A she-cat that makes loud breathing or purring sounds in sleep.
A depressed, elongated tract between two hills.
A sounding or murmuring spring, a running spring, or a spring welling forth abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sound or abundance of the flowing water motivates the designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of water or wind, or the rustling sound made by an eagle's wings in flight.
A plural designation for men coming from one town, country, or other place to another, and for those passing along, away, or by.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived plural usage associated with the active-participle family.
